pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Oklahoma Journeyman Electrician examination is part of the state electrical licensing process. Candidates preparing for this exam should follow the current Oklahoma Construction Industries Board application and testing instructions before scheduling. The licensing process may include application review, documentation of qualifying electrical experience or training, examination approval, and final license issuance requirements. The Oklahoma Journeyman Electrician exam is designed to measure whether the candidate understands the electrical knowledge required to work as a licensed journeyman electrician. Journeyman-level testing focuses on practical trade knowledge, code application, safety, wiring methods, calculations, and the ability to apply NEC rules to real installation scenarios.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Oklahoma journeyman electrician preparation should include the National Electrical Code, electrical theory, practical installation knowledge, conductor sizing, grounding and bonding, services, feeders, branch circuits, motors, transformers, wiring methods, raceways, boxes, overcurrent protection, special occupancies, special equipment, safety, and calculations. Candidates should also be prepared to review Oklahoma-specific electrical rules and licensing responsibilities when those topics are included in the exam materials or application instructions. Electrical calculations are an important part of journeyman-level preparation. Candidates should practice service load calculations, feeder calculations, branch-circuit calculations, conductor ampacity, conductor adjustment and correction, voltage drop, box fill, raceway fill, motor calculations, transformer calculations, demand factors, neutral loads, continuous loads, and overcurrent protection sizing. Calculation questions can be challenging under time pressure, so repeated practice is a key part of preparation.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: Oklahoma Journeyman Electrician exam preparation should include open-book code navigation and reference-use practice. Electrical licensing exams that test NEC knowledge require candidates to understand how the code is organized, how to locate tables, how to follow definitions, and how to apply the correct rule to the facts in a question. Even when references are allowed, candidates must be prepared before exam day. Open-book testing does not mean the answers are easy to find. Questions may require candidates to connect multiple code sections, understand definitions, apply table notes, recognize exceptions, complete calculations, and compare answer choices against the exact wording of the code. A candidate who is not comfortable using the NEC can spend too much time searching and lose focus during the exam. pieces.h: Q: Does this package include calculation practice?
pieces.t: Yes. The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide is included to help candidates review calculation topics that commonly appear on electrical contractor and master-level electrical exams.

pieces.h: Q: Does an Oklahoma electrical journeyman license allow contracting?
pieces.t: No. Electrical contracting is handled through Oklahoma electrical contractor licensing. Candidates who plan to contract for electrical work should review the contractor license category and requirements that apply to their work.

pieces.h: Q: Does this package guarantee that I will pass?
pieces.t: No. This package is designed to support preparation through organized study materials, code review, calculations practice, flash cards, online questions, and structured study guidance. Exam results depend on the candidate’s preparation, knowledge, and performance.

pieces.h: Q: Should I confirm Oklahoma licensing requirements before testing?
pieces.t: Yes. Candidates should confirm the required license category, eligibility requirements, application process, code edition, reference rules, and post-exam licensing steps before scheduling or taking an exam.

pieces.h: Q: Is this combo based on the 2026 NEC?
pieces.t: Yes. This combo is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code and includes the National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback.

pieces.h: Q: What books are included in this package?
pieces.t: This package includes the 2026 Oklahoma Master Electrician Study Guide, the 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide, and the National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback.

pieces.h: Q: Who should use this Oklahoma master electrician combo?
pieces.t: This combo is intended for electricians preparing for Oklahoma electrical contractor, master-level electrician, journeyman, NEC-based, open-book code navigation, and electrical calculation exam content.

pieces.h: Q: Who administers Oklahoma electrical licensing?
pieces.t: Oklahoma electrical licensing is administered through the Oklahoma Construction Industries Board.

pieces.h: Q: Who provides Oklahoma electrical exams?
pieces.t: PSI provides electrical testing services for Oklahoma candidates working through the Construction Industries Board examination program.

pieces.h: Q: Does Oklahoma use a master electrician license?
pieces.t: Oklahoma electrical licensing is commonly organized around contractor and journeyman classifications, including unlimited and residential categories. Candidates should confirm the exact license classification they need before applying.

pieces.h: Q: Does this package help with electrical calculations?
pieces.t: Yes. The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide is included to help candidates practice formulas, NEC table use, load calculations, conductor sizing, raceway fill, box fill, service calculations, and other calculation-based topics.

pieces.h: Q: Can I study directly from the NEC with this package?
pieces.t: Yes. The National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback is included so candidates can study article language, definitions, tables, exceptions, and code requirements directly.

pieces.h: Exam Room Approved Books
pieces.t: NFPA 70 National Electrical Code, 2023 Edition The current Oklahoma electrical exam bulletin lists the 2023 NEC, as revised and adopted by the Oklahoma Uniform Building Code Commission, as an approved reference for electrical exams. NEC Handbooks and spiral-bound NEC copies are not allowed in the test center. Code of Federal Regulations 29 CFR Part 1926 OSHA construction standards are listed as approved electrical exam reference material. Candidates may use the approved OSHA reference format listed in the current bulletin. Ugly’s Electrical References Ugly’s Electrical References is listed as an approved reference for Oklahoma electrical examinations and supports quick review of formulas, tables, conversions, and electrical reference information. State of Oklahoma Construction Industries Board Unofficial Administrative Rules & Courtesy Exam Study Aids Book This Oklahoma-specific reference is listed for business, law, and regulatory exam preparation and supports review of Construction Industries Board rules and study aids.

pieces.h: Exam Room Approved Books
pieces.t: Oklahoma Electrical Industry Regulations, Oklahoma Administrative Code, Title 158, Chapter 40 This reference contains Oklahoma electrical industry regulations and supports state-specific licensing and regulatory study. Oklahoma Electrical License Act, Oklahoma Statutes, Title 59, Chapter 40A This reference covers Oklahoma electrical licensing law and is useful for understanding contractor and journeyman responsibilities.

pieces.h: Q: Who is this Oklahoma Master Electrician exam prep combo for?
pieces.t: This combo is for electricians preparing for Oklahoma master-level electrical contractor exam preparation, including candidates studying for the Oklahoma Unlimited Electrical Contractor exam.

pieces.h: Q: Is this product based on the 2026 National Electrical Code?
pieces.t: Yes. This product is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code and is designed to support NEC-focused electrical exam preparation.

pieces.h: Q: Who regulates electrical licensing in Oklahoma?
pieces.t: Electrical licensing in Oklahoma is regulated by the Oklahoma Construction Industries Board.

pieces.h: Q: Is the Oklahoma Unlimited Electrical Contractor exam open book?
pieces.t: Yes. The Oklahoma Unlimited Electrical Contractor examination is an open book test with approved references allowed in the examination room.

pieces.h: Q: How many questions are on the Oklahoma Unlimited Electrical Contractor exam?
pieces.t: The Oklahoma Unlimited Electrical Contractor exam contains 100 scored items.

pieces.h: Q: How much time is allowed for the Oklahoma Unlimited Electrical Contractor exam?
pieces.t: The exam allows 240 minutes for completion.

pieces.h: Q: What references are allowed for the Oklahoma Unlimited Electrical Contractor exam?
pieces.t: Approved references include the National Electrical Code, Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926 or the PSI selections version, and Ugly’s Electrical References by George V. Hart.

pieces.h: Q: What experience is required for an Oklahoma Unlimited Electrical Contractor license?
pieces.t: Oklahoma requires 12,000 verifiable hours of on-the-job electrical construction experience, proof of 4,000 hours as a licensed Unlimited Electrical Journeyman, and 6,000 hours in commercial industrial work obtained while employed by a licensed Electrical Contractor. A maximum of 2,000 hours may be satisfied by formal electrical education.

pieces.h: Q: Does this product include practice exams?
pieces.t: Yes. This package includes 12 practice exams plus 2 full final exams. The practice exams help you build familiarity with exam-style questions, while the final exams help you evaluate readiness after completing more of your study plan.

pieces.h: Q: Are flash cards included?
pieces.t: Yes. This is a study guide and flash card combo. The flash cards are designed to help reinforce electrical terms, formulas, definitions, NEC concepts, Oklahoma regulations, safety topics, calculations, and exam-style recall.

pieces.h: Q: Does this combo guarantee that I will pass the exam?
pieces.t: No. This product is designed to support preparation through structured study, practice exams, final exams, flash card review, reference navigation, and NEC-based preparation. Exam results and licensing approval depend on the candidate’s preparation, testing performance, and Oklahoma licensing requirements.
